subject: humanities
passage: The yo-yo is often called one of the oldest toys in the world, and a disk on a string that climbs back up appears on a Greek vase painted around 440 BCE. The modern toy, though, owes its name and its most important feature to the Philippines. Pedro Flores, a Filipino immigrant who started making yo-yos in California in ______ used a string looped loosely around the axle instead of tied to it, so the yo-yo could spin at the end of the string before climbing back up. A businessman named Donald Duncan bought his company within two years, and the trick-friendly design spread around the world.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A Filipino immigrant who started making yo-yos in California in 1928" is extra information about Pedro Flores. It opens with a comma after "Flores," so it must close with a comma before the verb "used."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Pedro Flores" from its verb "used."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause; it can't separate the subject "Pedro Flores" from its verb "used."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "used."
explanation.D: Correct. The closing comma matches the opening comma after "Flores" and completes the pair around the extra information.
